newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW--US July industrial output up 0.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW--US July industrial output up 0.2 pct.

text.p: Following are comments from U.S. economists after the Federal Reserve said industrial production rose 0.2 percent in July against a revised 0.3 percent rise in June. Capacity utilization fell to 83.1 percent against 83.3 percent earlier.
Economists in a Reuters survey had expected a 0.2 percent rise in industrial production and a 83.5 percent reading on the capacity utilization data.

NANCY KIMELMAN, ECONOMIST, TECHNICAL DATA: "(Economic) data have been coming pretty much on target today and these industrial figures play right into where we think the economy is, specifically the factory sector."

LOU CRANDALL, CHIEF ECONOMIST , R.H. WRIGHTSON AND ASSOCIATES, iNC.: "With capacity utilization down to 83.1 percent, we are even further away from the inflationary pressure point than we were before this release. This will not do anything to change the Federal Reserve's view.

He said the drop in the capacity utilization rate occurred despite a weather-related 1.5-percent surge in the utilities industry's component. "Definitely, nothing inflationary in that report," he said.

JOHN WILLIAMS, MANAGING DIRECTOR AND CHIEF GLOBAL MARKETS ECONOMIST, BANKERS TRUST CO: "This is a very favorable set of statistics. Industrial production for June was up 0.2 percent with a downward revision to the May figure of 0.2 percent.

"That means capacity utilization has actuallly fallen off to 83.1 percent, which is the lowest that it has been this year. For those looking for signs of inflation pressure, they should be happy to see that capacity utilization is actually at the lowest level of the year thanks to the downward revision of industrial production in May.
"These are very modest figures -- very much in line with expections -- although the capacity utilization number is probably better than expected."
